segments.text: The Delhi demolitions, is it too little, too late?
Why wait for tragedies to act?
Demolitions and exercise in tokenism?
Who will crack down on the corruption at the municipal level?
Joining me now, Jagdish Maamgen is a former MCD chairman and an ex-chairman, the VC Selection Committee at Kota University.
Ellen Rao, former DCP, Delhi, joins me.
And Sridhar Pabisetti, urban governance and public policy expert.
Good to have all of you on the show.
Mr. Maamgen, I must come to you first.
Because at the end of the day, the buck surely at some level stops with MCD.
At least as you saw in the story, everyone blames the MCD.
Saying bribe lette hain, allow these permissions to go on.
And even the governments will hold MCD accountable even though they should be reporting to the government of the day.
Is MCD the real villain or the soft target?
Actually in this case, there are more than one villain.
The illegal construction for that MCD is villain definitely, but the non availability of PG's, non availability of hostels in Delhi University Colleges

for that the university is also a villain but nobody is talking about the university or nobody is talking about the colleges who has not made the hostel so that children are forced to get these PGs and
No, I take your point, sir.
I take your point.
The huge mismatch.
In fact, the figures are shocking.
Barely 2.77% of the total population of the Delhi University students actually get accommodation from the colleges.
That's just 2.77%.
But the MCD itself, let's talk about that villain.
Today, suddenly illegal buildings are being demolished.
Did it take a tragedy for them to wake up?
And now Rekha Gupta is there, going from place to place.
She and her government, everyone knows that there is a Neta Babu contractor nexus.
This should have been broken before.
Where is the system failing, sir?
Rajdeepji, it's just I was... You must remember that when Malvenagar fire incident happened, then also Rekha Gupta government said, we will crack down on ground plus four.
What happened?
In Hausrani, there are many buildings which are five floors, six floors.
Anyone is cracked down.
And after Saidullah job also, they said we will crack down.
And after this, now Satyariketan also, they are saying we will crack down.
First of all is that the government has nothing to do with it.
It is MCD to do with it.
And MCD comes under Union Home Ministry.
It doesn't come under the government.
They are just playing with the sentiments of the people.
We are suspending five officers.
Chief Minister can suspend even a peon.
Delhi Chief Minister has the right to suspend a peon.
It is MCD commissioner or LG or Home Ministry that can suspend any officer of the MCD.
So this is just an eye wash and it is a political gimmick.
I'm glad that there is someone.
It has happened.
I'm glad you're speaking.
They are announcing something and this about PG rules.
Yesterday High Court has directed them to make a regulation for the PG.
It is not their choice, it is not their opinion.
It is High Court has directed MCD and Delhi Government and DDA to make a regulation for the PG's.
Okay, I take your point sir.
You are making very strong points and I am glad that someone is speaking so plainly about it.
Whether the MCD is accountable, as you said, they are accountable to the Home Ministry, the LG, and not to the Delhi government per se.
The truth of the matter, Ellen Rao, you're a former DCP, Delhi, why does it take debt to trigger enforcement?
Delhi has recorded roughly 169 deaths, sir, from building collapse incidents between 2020 and 2024, according to NCRB linked data.
Did it take this tragedy?
for the system to wake up.
The police officers in the local areas will also know whether there is a building being built illegally.
Why don't they act?
Good evening, Rajiv, and to all your viewers, my co-panelists, and really the data which has been given by you is shocking data.
causing the death of so many people and building collapsed.
And the main reason is that we have the tendency of forgetting all these things.
We recently got to know about the fire incident of Maliyu Nagar and the students.
The basement was flooded with water during rainy season and so on.
So many other incidents are there, no doubt.
But every time there is an Inquiry Commission is there, no doubt.
And then the Inquiry Commission suggests some remedies for the things that should not happen in the future.
But still it's going on.
I don't think that there is... What's the role of the police here?
What's the role of the police?
Rajeev, I'm coming to that also, but let me make the background of that.
No doubt that these vulnerabilities are to be checked mainly by the MCD and because that comes under the building department of MCD.
But nevertheless, the police is also having some responsibility to inform the MNCD about such illegal activities.
There are circular by the Commissioner of Police that police will not interfere in the illegal construction in their area.
But at the same time, they have been instructed to inform the concerned department
to inform the MCD about such irregularity.

But if the police has done in that, they have done their duty by informing the concerned MCD officials that such and such building is being constructed without any building bylaws, violating the building bylaws without any
That is important.
In this case, I think the police is investigating whether that information was provided to the MCD or not.
If it was not provided, then definitely the police is responsible for this.
Sir, I take your point again.
You see, the problem is we all, it's after the event that we realized where the system, you know, everyone sort of passes the buck.
It's a famous Indian sport, if I may call it unfortunate.
Sridhar, Pabhi said T, you tell us, is there a solution?
We all know the problem.
Give me a solution.
Is demolishing five buildings today actually only an exercise in tokenism?
Yeah, I mean, it's not only five buildings who are life threatening in the city of Delhi.
There could be 500, there could be 5,000, there could be 50,000.
I was on the panel discussion yesterday and one gentleman said one in five buildings in Delhi are unsafe.
Right.
So it's important for us to now begin the journey of first classifying safe and unsafe buildings.
Then we can go on to the journey of illegal and legal buildings, right?
The legally illegal buildings is for the government of the day to put the laws together, but safe and safe is not something that we have the luxury to wait.
This is something that has to be taken upon a war footing.
I remember in Bengaluru, when there was a very efficient special commissioner, he ended up giving
the urban property records, one lakh records in every month for a continuous series of months back to back.
So we have technology that today enables us to visualize our cities through satellites, through other drones and other things.
Now with this, can't we designate and identify the
unsafe buildings by bringing together knowledge across departments.

The fire safety is the one which will definitely know any buildings that are more than five stories high, which does not have enough area for the fire engine to go inside and which can be dangerous in case of a fire accident.
the public works department and the sewage department knows the flood prone areas of Delhi.
So, it's a recurrence of these series of things building collapses, fire,
and even flooding.
All these three things can be prevented only when you create a database of all the buildings and classify them into safe and safe.
And every single day from now on, we should go after and reduce these unsafe buildings.
We should give them a way of people to move to temporary transit housing.
We should make sure that their dignity is maintained while this process is taken care of.
Maybe what we need is like my first guest today was the FDA commissioner of Mumbai.
He has put fear and ensuring compliance as a result.
Maybe you need a strong man at the top.
who will take on the politicians, who will question the MCD officials, who will also be able to control what's happening on the ground.
This Neta Babu contractor nexus needs to be broken.
And yes, the university also needs to get its act together.
But you need people who are strong with a spine at the top.
We are seeing it happening with the FDA commissioner in Mumbai.
Maybe Delhi also needs someone like that.
I appreciate my guests joining me on my other talking point tonight.
Thank you all very much.
